Israeli officials say results stand as Netanyahu claims election 'stolen' (2 Nov 2026)
Central Elections Committee head Noam Sohlberg stated: "Our position is that even if the suspicions are substantiated, this would not undermine the integrity of the electoral process."
Netanyahu's Likud party alleged without evidence that Arab-led parties "stole" the vote and received funding from Qatar. Qatar has rejected these accusations as disinformation.
Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats; Eisenkot's bloc 48 in the 120-seat parliament. Arab-led parties won a record 19 seats, enough to give Eisenkot a 67-seat majority if he forms a coalition with them.
Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of conducting an "orchestrated and organised campaign to delegitimise the results." Eisenkot previously rejected coalition partnerships with Arab parties.
Police arrested political activists carrying cash allegedly for voter bribes, reportedly connected to the Ra'am party, which won eight seats. Party leader Mansour Abbas called the arrests an "attempt to influence the election results."
Official certification of results is expected this week, after which President Isaac Herzog will nominate a candidate to form a government.
